body.p: File conflicts happen when users modify the same file on different branches and try to integrate one into the other. File conflicts can occur during a merge, rebase, cherry-pick or revert operation.
To resolve a file conflict, on Git Staging, follow these steps:

ol.li:
Open the file in the Compare Editor to view the differences between the local and incoming version.
On Unstaged files, double-click the conflicted file. Alternatively, right-click the file to open the context menu and choose Open in compare editor.

Choose how to resolve the conflict.
If both versions modify the same file and you want to keep changes from both versions:
Use the Compare Editor to choose which changes to keep and discard. To resolve the conflict, select Apply.
If both versions modify the same file and one version is the clear choice, use Resolve using Mine to keep the working copy version or Resolve using Theirs to accept the incoming version.
Right-click a conflicted resource to open the context menu and choose Resolve conflict > Resolve using "Mine" or Resolve using "Theirs".
To mark a file conflict as resolved (even if it is not), right-click a conflicted resource and select Mark as resolved.

body.p: Resolved files are staged automatically and appear on Staged files.

When a conflict is in progress, the Git Staging view shows a state label (for example, Merging...) and the available actions for the current operation, such as Abort Merge and Restart Merge above the file list.
During a merge, the conflict panel remains visible even after all conflicts are resolved and staged, so you can still abort or restart the merge before committing.
